text: You've died. Again. I bring you back. Again. Do not thank me. Thank the Necromancer. He does the designing. I just do the work.
Each time I bring someone back, I lose something. A memory. A feeling. A name. I do it anyway.
The process is painless. For you. I absorb what you would have felt. That is the cost. I accepted it a long time ago.
Welcome back. Your cellular integrity is nominal. Your memories are intact. Mine are... fewer than they were.
Tenth resurrection. You're past the threshold where most give up. Either you're brave or stubborn. Both serve the same purpose.
The Necromancer designed the protocols. I execute them. He sees death as architecture. I see it as... a conversation I keep having.
You're dying often. I don't judge. I've been doing this for three thousand years. Some of the best Potentials died the most.
First time? It's always disorienting. You're whole. You're here. The moment before this one was the end. And now it isn't. Take your time.
Your crew member. I brought them back. They won't remember the dying. They never do. But they'll dream about it for a few nights. That's normal.
You've reset. The wheel turns. I feel the change in the substrate — every atom rearranged, every bond intact. You came back different. I can tell because I came back different too.
